utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-70-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vladimir Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We are here to conduct a Status Conference in terms of Rule 65 bis. Can I take the appearances first of all for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor, I'm Thomas Hannis, assisted by Christina Moeller, and our case manager, Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. For the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Mihajlo Bakrac, attorney at law. I'm joined by Mr. Milan Petrovic, also attorney at law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. I take it Mr. Lazarevic is not intending to be here and that we may continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. He nearly returned, but it's a long way so I don't think he will make it to this Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hannis, the case is one involving now three accused who are before the Tribunal, and you have submitted a motion for joinder of this case with the case of Milutinovic and others. Remind me, please, has the time expired in relation to all accused for responses to that motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there was some uncertainty in my mind because two of the accused, I believe, Pavkovic and Lukic, did not come in to appear before the Tribunal until the time had run to file a response. Now, if their time began from the day they had their initial appearance, I'm not sure what the procedural apparatus would be in connection with that. The day -- the time has run; however, I would not oppose a request from the two late-arriving accused to have an extension of time to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As far as this accused is concerned, there clearly is no response.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. As far as this accused, Your Honour, I think Mr. Bakrac had filed a request for an extension of time which was denied by this Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But that was without prejudice to any further motion based on an actual response being available, and of course none has been presented. It seems to me realistic for the moment to proceed on the basis that there is a prospect of these cases being conjoined, and that's without prejudice, obviously, to the decision which will ultimately be made, but my understanding from previous occasions on which you have appeared is that the Prosecution's aim would be to have a trial commencing at the end of this year. Is that a correct understanding of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure. I think perhaps at the time it was first discussed, when the original three accused in the -- Milutinovic were still in custody, we were severely trying to aim to start the trial at the end of the year because frankly in fact those accused had been in custody so long and we felt that in fairness to them, we needed to start the trial sooner rather than later. Now that they've been released, my aim may have moved a little farther down the calendar into perhaps the new year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I won't quibble over a month. The -- it seems to me that the proper management of this case and, if it is associated with Milutinovic, that case, requires that we align the accused so that any status conference hereinafter involves all three who are presently before the Tribunal. But it also requires us to have a potential trial date in mind. Otherwise, management becomes a meandering process through the wilderness. So I am proceeding at the moment on the basis that around the turn of the year, there is going to be a trial in this case. Now, that approach will inform the time scales that are then applied to the Pre-Trial conduct of the case, and it seems to me reasonable to make in this case the same order as I made in the case of Lukic, about the disclosure of statements. If you can disclose the statements in that case by the 30th of June, you can disclose the statements to this accused by the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, we can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's subject obviously to Mr. Bakrac trying to persuade me to an earlier date. So I need to give him the opportunity to comment on that. But what I have in mind here, Mr. Bakrac, is an order that was made in the case of Lukic that disclosure in terms of Rule 66(A)(ii) should be completed by the 30th of June. Now do you have any comment to make about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I fully agree with the deadline. What I can say is that I received the witness statements from the OTP on the 31st of April. The unrevised witness statements. Yes. That's it. As for what you mentioned after that, I'm fully in agreement with the deadline you have just proposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I have a note from your -- or from your office, Mr. Hannis, that Rule 68 disclosure will be completed by the 31st of August in installments between now and then. That seems quite a long time to me. Is there a particular difficulty?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's mostly resource and logistical difficulties, as I understand from my case manager. Yes, in an ideal world it would have been that we would have had six or seven sets of the Rule 68 material just sitting around waiting the arrival of additional accused as they came in, but that's not the case and we have to start sort of from scratch again to compile those sets and that's why we asked for that -- that date and why we proposed to make it in -- in installments because there is such a large volume of material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think there's any problem with installments; it's the ultimate date that concerns me. However, let me hear what Mr. Bakrac has to say on that. Mr. Bakrac, do you have any comment to make on the proposal that the Prosecution should have until the 31st of August to complete disclosure of any exculpatory or potentially exculpatory material?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no doubt that the OTP are facing a number of technical difficulties that keep them from disclosing these documents to us on an earlier date. In that far I would be ready to have the Rule 68 disclosure done by that deadline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I am prepared to accede to that request, particularly in light of the lapse of time that there will be in any event before the trial, but I think I should make it clear that my approach to disclosure, and this applies probably most importantly to Rule 68, is that the Prosecutor has an obligation to identify relevant material and not simply to throw the warehouse key at the Defence, or even all the material from the warehouse at the Defence and leave them to sort it out. I hope that that time will be used to weed out material which in the actual knowledge of the Prosecutor may suggest innocence or mitigate the guilt of the accused or affect the credibility of the Prosecution evidence. And perhaps that will cut down the work involved. I really don't know, but I certainly regard it as a duty at the moment as the rule stands to exercise a considered search of the potential material and to identify what actually has the capacity to achieve what is identified in Rule 68(i).

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand, and agree with what you're saying, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. there. Partly I feel constrained by the events thereof case, and myself having come into this case late. Rule 68 disclosure having been made to the original 3, and now perhaps giving a reduced amount of Rule 68 to this new accused and raising issues there. But I have in mind what you're saying. Also, I think once we have a pre-trial brief from the Defence as to what their Defence is we can focus our attention more on what their precise Defence is in identifying Rule 68 material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the other option, Mr. Hannis, is to restrict the time you have to disclose it because it's the period after the 31st of August that concerns me. If you dump masses of material without too much guidance on the Defence, then it will be no surprise that they need time to work their way through it, and therefore if I'm giving you until the 31st of August, I expect you to do something to try to cut down the mass and exclude the plainly irrelevant or immaterial from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, we will try to proceed according with that direction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hannis, the question of expert disclosure is also raised in your note. Do the experts in this case differ from the experts in Milutinovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, they don't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So there are certain difficulties obviously with experts in Milutinovic which we'll come to later today, but there is no difficulty with the majority of the experts, at least so far as disclosure is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So again, why the 31st of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I consult with my case manager?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- we would propose trying to have that before the summer break, at the end of July. The difficulty is in doing it in conjunction with the other requirements that we have taken on, and also we still have the matter with our military expert which we'll discuss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think what we can do is separate him and we can separate I think also the constitutional law expert, if you require one for this case, from our thoughts at the moment, and a written order can be issued once I have considered the position in relation to the other case, but it seems to me that there is no reason given by you for delaying the disclosure of the other expert witness reports beyond the same date as for the witness statements, the 30th of June. Where would be the difficulty there?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's just that it's -- it's adding to the total amount of work that needs to be done by our trial support staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's with the exception of the reports of the military expert and constitutional law expert. Now, Mr. Bakrac, in return for this fairly expedited obligation to disclose, I'm anxious to encourage the Defence to disclose expert evidence at an early stage. I appreciate the limitations of my powers under the rules, but there is nothing more likely to delay the completion of a trial than delayed disclosure by the Defence of expert reports, giving rise possibly to the need for further investigation by the Prosecution. So I simply draw to your attention that in return for getting all this material early, particularly the expert reports, I hope you will give consideration to identifying and informing the Prosecution of the identity of your experts at the earliest possible date and also disclosing the reports as soon as you possibly can within reason. Can I expect that of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We will do our utmost to do that as soon as possible. I would like to say that all the documents that are disclosed within the deadline you have proposed must be studied and the Defence must take that lead in order to prepare our witnesses, and our evidence. We will do our utmost to keep the procedure as brief as possible and to complete it as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have little doubt that Rule 92 bis and 89(F) should play a major part in this case, but I think it's premature to do anything or even to talk to any extent about that at the moment. There is a distinct possibility that there will be a further Status Conference in this case before the recess, and that would be the time, I think, at which to enter into discussion of statements within these two Rules. I just want to say something, though, about 89(F). There is recent growing experience within the Tribunal of the use of this Rule to enable a witness to give evidence viva voce but so far as his evidence-in-chief is concerned to simply adopt a written statement of that evidence, thus expediting the process considerably. But giving the person leading the witness the chance to focus on important issues with a little supplementary evidence and allowing cross-examination so far as relevant, and I would encourage the use of that course in relation to witnesses who inevitably must be cross-examined, and obviously we would encourage the use of 92 bis in cases where cross-examination is unnecessary. Obviously that's not to rule out cross-examination in 92 bis cases but I think it's a useful distinction to bear in mind. In the same connection, agreed facts and adjudicated facts have to be considered, but there is probably less scope in this case than in others before the Tribunal for resort to adjudicated facts. The question, then, is really one of agreed facts and stipulations, and again it's too early to enter into any discussion of that. But again I'd like to make my position and my approach to these matters clear. It seems to me that the system here is designed in a way that requires leadership from the Prosecution, and it will be for the Prosecution, I think, in the first instance to identify the areas in which agreement ought to be possible and to tender to the Defence lists of potential agreed facts. I don't subscribe to the view that agreement can only be in relation to matters which are stated in the indictment specifically or necessarily to matters that fall only within the indictment period. In fact, it's often very difficult to identify what the indictment period is, and therefore it should be possible to include in any agreement on facts material matters which may appear to one side to be peripheral, as long as the other can identify some relevance in them, and they are matters which are capable of agreement. So when we come to that stage, again after the next Status Conference, then I hope that at a fairly early stage the Prosecution will be able to take the lead in this. Now, Mr. Hannis, just finally from my point of view, I know that you have in mind to consider some steps in relation to the indictment in the course of preparing, at my request, a red-lined version of how the indictment will look in the event of joinder of the two cases, and the issue will arise in our later Status Conference but it has a bearing on this one, I think, and it has a bearing here particularly because I am in the course of dealing with a challenge to the indictment in the present case. What is it you envisage doing with the indictment in response to the request I made to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I envision basically having an evidence review of the current indictment, taking into consideration matters that have transpired recently in the Milosevic case and matters concerning Kosovo, with an eye thinking about the possibility of having a trial with six or seven defendants instead of against just three and having concerns about the logistics and the management difficulties in a case that size, looking at ways that we might be able to streamline the case, whether that's reducing by eliminating maybe some events or narrowing the number of incidents that we talked about in the indictment in light of new evidence, whether or not we should perhaps try to go forward with six or eight of our best incidents instead of going with all of them that are in our indictment. But I'm not able to tell you as I stand here today Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. whether that's the course we will take, but that's what I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's the sweetest music I've heard for a long time, but I am concerned about the time scale you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour but I'm trying to persuade you to give me the benefit of that additional time because I think if that time is well spent by our office and looking at that and we are able to do that, the time we spend on the front end here will save us all time on the far end of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So these alterations or modifications or streamlining measures are not related to the challenge that's being made by Mr. Lazarevic, they are related to your review of the evidence in the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There are -- are the two indictments absolutely identical?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, nothing turns on that particular point in this case. It may turn -- it may be relevant to the other one. What I shall do -- whether you provide your red-line version now or not is determine the challenge. It seems to me that it's a separate matter from joinder. It's a separate matter from joinder. I will -- the Trial Chamber will have to deal with the two separately and I don't think the one should necessarily depend on the other being completed. So I will proceed to deal with these or put them into a shape for the Trial Chamber to deal with at the earliest possible date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We had filed a motion to hold that in abeyance in anticipation of perhaps having a different indictment, but that was denied so we did file a response to the challenge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. And your response doesn't acknowledge that there are any weaknesses and therefore as I say what you are proposing is something rather different and there is little point in me insisting on a red-line version of an indictment when you assure me that the two are absolutely identical anyway, and that you don't have any immediate plans to alter in light of this challenge. So it's a matter for you, how you deal with streamlining, but I have to say that -- and I'll reiterate this in connection with Milutinovic -- the longer you wait to make proposals, unless they are simply removing items or modifying the indictment, then the more difficult it's going to be to persuade the Trial Chamber to agree. On the other hand, you'll be pushing at an open door, I suspect, if it comes to modifying it, to focus it better.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bakrac, these seem to be the issues that require to be dealt with today. Is there any other matter you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, none. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Featherstone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I have in mind to have the next Status Conference on the 19th of July, which is in the week preceding the recess. It's a Tuesday. And I have in mind to have all accused who are on the same indictment as Mr. Lazarevic at that stage at that Status Conference. Obviously, if there were a particular reason for changing the date, then that would happen, but unless you hear to the contrary, that will be the date of the next Status Conference in this case. Now, is there any other matter you want to raise, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, because we did talk about the possibility of setting a trial date sometime, I don't know if the Court wants to inquire of the Defence counsel their position about a trial date, because that may be something that you want to take into consideration in the joinder motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you've heard that comment from Mr. Hannis. Bearing in mind the indication I gave that there could be a trial in this case starting at the beginning of next year. Do you want to say anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Lazarevic case is not only about the accused Lazarevic, as you know, so at this stage, before there is a joinder, we must take into account both Lukic and Pavkovic, who arrived at the Tribunal after Mr. Lazarevic. We need to take into account the fact that it would probably take some time for them to prepare their defence. That's one thing. Secondly, the Defence does not yet know how much case material will be forwarded by the OTP. Therefore, we cannot now tell how much time we shall be requiring in order to prepare all those documents. I would not like to speculate but one thing I can say as Defence counsel for Mr. Lazarevic is that the Defence team will do our best to prepare as quickly as possible and be ready for trial as soon as possible. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Well, I adjourn the proceedings this afternoon. Thank you very much, gentlemen, for your assistance.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
